title: Syre’s $1 bn Vietnam plan: Can textile-to-textile recycling scale?
content:
Syre is reviewing its $1 billion Vietnam recycled polyester project, while still envisaging a 150,000-tonne facility.
The Nhon Hoi project received an investment certificate in June 2025 and was announced with 250,000 tonnes of annual output.
Feedstock needs of 300,000-400,000 tonnes exceed expected domestic discarded-fabric supply; Vietnam’s permitted-scrap list does not list textile waste.

title: South India cotton yarn prices stable, post-Diwali demand weak
content:
Mumbai and Tiruppur cotton yarn prices stayed stable as post-Diwali buyers delayed purchases and downstream units remained below normal operations.
Tight payment flows kept trade thin across the textile value chain, while traders expect buying and replenishment to improve next week.
Gujarat cotton prices were unchanged on lower kapas arrivals; all-India arrivals were put at 80,000–82,000 bales.

title: Bata India chases younger consumers with sneakers and premium lines
content:
Bata India is targeting younger consumers through sneakers, premium lines and consumer-led stores to sustain sales growth.
Quarterly turnover grew 7.5 per cent to ₹861.8 crore (~$91.6 million), as higher price points lifted prices and footfall.
Franchisee, institutional and distribution channels grew double digits; e-commerce grew and adjusted profit before tax rose over 31 per cent.

title: US cotton futures edge higher on export demand, firm dollar caps gains
content:
US cotton futures settled marginally higher on Thursday, with March 2027 on ICE Futures US up 0.15 per cent at 82.51 cents per pound, supported by recent strong export sales.
A stronger US dollar, weaker Chicago grains and harvest pressure capped gains, while USDA cut US output to 13.18 million bales.
Traders await the delayed USDA export sales report; ICE-certified stocks rose to 76,570 bales.

title: Bangladesh's garment factories shut amid protests over wage hike
content:
Wage protests have halted more than 100 garment factories in Gazipur, Ashulia and Savar, with 11 units announcing indefinite closures ahead of Bangladesh's minimum wage talks.
Workers proposed Tk32,000 (~$256) a month, while employers may submit a proposal but boycott Monday's Minimum Wage Board meeting.
RMG accounts for around 80 per cent of Bangladesh's $48 billion in annual exports.

title: US’ Wolverine posts eighth consecutive quarter of growth in Q3 FY26
content:
Wolverine World Wide has raised its FY26 outlook after third-quarter revenue rose 7.5 per cent to $505.4 million and net earnings attributable to the company reached $65.8 million.
Operating margin expanded to 17.7 per cent, aided by $35.3 million in IEEPA tariff refunds.
The footwear and apparel group now expects FY26 revenue of $2.00-$2.01 billion and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.95-$1.99.

title: India's $1 bn US apparel gap: Can exporters win back buyers?
content:
TexPro found India's US apparel imports fell $1.014 billion in January-August 2026, down 25.96 per cent as the market slipped 7.02 per cent.
Its share fell to 5.59 per cent from 7.02 per cent, while Vietnam and Cambodia gained and knitted apparel led losses.
Talks may ease clearance, but no apparel-specific tariff relief is confirmed; recovery hinges on price, delivery and policy stability.
